stories.title: Development and external validation of a predictive model for epithelial ovarian tumors based on MRI features and serum tumor markers
stories.description: Ovarian cancer remains a major threat to women’s health, and early-stage disease is often asymptomatic, making timely diagnosis difficult. This study aimed to develop and externally validate a predictive model integrating magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features and serum tumor markers to distinguish benign from malignant epithelial ovarian tumors. A total of 222 patients from Huzhou Maternity & Child Health Care Hospital were included as the training cohort, and 102 patients from Sir Run Run Shaw Hospital served as the external validation cohort. Independent predictors were identified using multivariate logistic regression, and a predictive model was constructed based on regression coefficients and externally validated. In the training cohort, 168 patients were benign and 54 were malignant. Tumor morphology, diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) signal intensity, ascites, carbohydrate antigen 125 (CA125), and human epididymis protein 4 (HE4) were independent predictors (AUCs: 0.748–0.876). The combined model achieved an AUC of 0.965, with 94.4% sensitivity and 84.5% specificity, and showed good calibration (P = 0.870). In the validation cohort (80 benign, 22 malignant), the model yielded an AUC of 0.972, with 90.9% sensitivity and 95.0% specificity. The proposed model integrating MRI features and serum tumor markers demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance and robust external validity. This practical and easily applicable tool may assist in preoperative risk stratification and clinical decision-making.

stories.title: Changes in breast cancer management and care infrastructure in Turki̇ye: a ten-year multicenter comparison, 2009-2019
stories.description: To evaluate changes in breast cancer management infrastructure, diagnostic approaches, and treatment practices in tertiary breast centers in Turkiye between 2009 and 2019 and identify areas requiring further development. This repeated cross-sectional multicenter institutional survey compared aggregated center-level data from 2009 to 2019. Data included pathologically confirmed breast cancer cases, diagnostic sampling, stage at diagnosis, breast and axillary surgery, neoadjuvant therapy, imaging availability, and specialized multidisciplinary and supportive-care services. Individual recurrence and survival outcomes were unavailable. Thirty-eight centers contributed data in 2009 and 44 in 2019, with confirmed cases increasing from 4,808 to 6,550 (p < 0.001). The number of specialized breast surgeons increased. Core needle biopsy largely replaced excisional/incisional diagnostic procedures (p < 0.001), while neoadjuvant therapy use increased (p < 0.001). Surgical management shifted toward breast-conserving surgery. The reported proportion of sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) increased from approximately 48% to 55%; however, the aggregated dataset did not include clinical nodal status or patient-level indications for SLNB, so appropriateness of axillary staging cannot be assessed. Availability of diagnostic imaging, medical oncology/chemotherapy units, and lymphedema services also improved, although progress remained uneven across multidisciplinary and supportive-care domains. Participating Turkish tertiary breast centers demonstrated substantial structural and procedural changes between 2009 and 2019 that were broadly consistent with evolving breast cancer care. Because patient-level treatment indications and longitudinal outcomes were unavailable, the appropriateness of individual axillary procedures and effects on disease-free or overall survival cannot be determined.

stories.title: Serial multi‑time‑point assessments of well‑defined somatosensory domains and their associations with limb spasticity after ischemic stroke
stories.description: The association between post-stroke somatosensory deficits and limb spasticity has been reported. This study aimed to assess patients at multiple time points to further investigate relationships between well-defined somatosensory domains and the occurrence of limb spasticity following ischemic stroke. Briefly, the study enrolled 514 patients with ischemic stroke. Post-stroke proprioceptive deficits, pain-temperature deficits, sensory extinction, and stereognosis deficits were evaluated at 10, 20, and 30 days post-discharge. Limb spasticity was assessed using the Modified Ashworth Scale at 30 and 90 days post-discharge; a score ≥ 1 was defined as spasticity. Multivariate logistic regression models were applied to examine relationships between these variables. The results showed that proprioceptive deficits and pain-temperature deficits at 10, 20, and 30 days post-discharge were associated with limb spasticity and moderate-to-severe limb spasticity (relative to mild spasticity), and an interaction was observed between these two deficits. Only post‑stroke sensory extinction and stereognosis deficits assessed at 10 days post‑discharge were associated with spasticity, but these associations were attenuated to non‑significance upon additional adjustment for admission affected‑limb muscle strength. In conclusion, proprioceptive and pain-temperature deficits at all three time points were associated with limb spasticity after ischemic stroke in this cohort. These findings guide future stroke‑somatosensory research.
